title: Suki, UpToDate bring AI clinical decision support into patient visits
key_facts: Suki, a health-care AI company, and Wolters Kluwer Health are launching Ask, a clinical decision support tool (software that offers doctors evidence-based advice) powered by UpToDate Expert AI.
UpToDate is a medical reference used by more than 3 million clinicians worldwide.
Ask lets physicians retrieve patient information and consult medical evidence inside the Suki for Clinicians app, without switching applications.
Ask becomes available this week across Epic, Oracle Health, athenahealth and MEDITECH for Suki's more than 400 health system and health tech customers.
In early evaluations, clinicians preferred answers with Suki's patient context 83 percent of the time, according to a joint news release; the evaluations did not establish whether outcomes improve.
Wolters Kluwer's Yaw Fellin says the physician remains responsible for clinical decisions and that drug dosing is a high-stakes area.
quote_evidence: In early evaluations, clinicians preferred responses incorporating Suki-supplied patient context over those without it 83 percent of the time, according to a joint news release shared with Newsweek.
The evaluations did not establish whether the integration improves clinical outcomes.
why_it_matters_hint: AI advice inside doctors' visit software could help clinicians, but the 83 percent figure is the companies' own and says nothing about patient outcomes.
notes: Newsweek Pro health-care page; facts come from the companies and a joint release shared with Newsweek. Punit Soni is Suki's founder and chief executive; Yaw Fellin is senior vice president and general manager of clinical decision support at Wolters Kluwer Health.
